name: NYSE TICK and advance-decline breadth as an intraday signal for US index trading
source_url: https://www.cxoadvisory.com/?p=30213 (CXO breadth study, daily US breadth 2003-2017); https://www.ebsco.com/articles/business-and-management/0252f6b4-ed01-5be8-8544-9c13b6170788/the-use-of-index-specific-market-breadth-and-index-over-moving-average-indicators-in-stock-trading-strategies (Yu, Webb and Lin, Journal of Investing 2025, abstract only); https://sentimentrader.com/blog/tick-shows-record-buying-pressure (practitioner TICK observations); Tim Ord TICK method in Stocks & Commodities vol 10 no 12 (no URL found) [uncertain]
author_year: Tim Ord (Stocks & Commodities, vol 10 no 12, early 1990s) for the TICK rule; Yu, Webb and Lin (2025) for breadth ratios; CXO Advisory breadth analysis (publication year not confirmed) [uncertain]
instrument: NYSE TICK ($TICK) and NYSE advance-decline line. No broker CFD for these found. A Maven MT5 price proxy (US500/US100 CFD) can be used for price, but breadth itself is not in MT5 [uncertain: Maven symbol list not checked]
timeframe: Intraday TICK readings (1 to 5 minutes in community scripts, e.g. a 1-minute SPY scalper). Zweig Breadth Thrust uses daily breadth
entry_rule: Ord rule as summarized by a secondary source: buy when two intraday TICK readings of about 600 or more downticks occur at approximately the same price level on the DJIA; sell is the mirror image [uncertain: exact wording and thresholds not verified against the original article]. Practitioner heuristics (readings within +/-400 are noise; +/-1000 is strong; fade extremes on range days) are unverified. Zweig Breadth Thrust: 10-day smoothed advances/(advances+declines) moves from below 0.40 to above 0.615 within 10 trading days
exit_rule: Not specified in the sources reviewed [uncertain]
stop_rule: Not specified in the sources reviewed [uncertain]
holding_time: Intraday for TICK rules; not specified [uncertain]. Zweig Breadth Thrust holds are multi-week in practitioner write-ups [uncertain]
trades_per_year: Not reported. Zweig Breadth Thrust: about 25 signals in 87 years (10 great, 3 meh, 12 horrible, per McClellan) [uncertain for TICK]
overnight_weekend: Not specified; intraday TICK use implies flat at close [uncertain]
signal_window_definition: TICK is the instantaneous count of NYSE upticks minus downticks; the session window (09:30-16:00 ET) and DST mapping are not addressed in any source found [uncertain]
sample_period: No rigorous TICK sample found. Ord: early 1990s description, no results shown. CXO: daily US breadth May 2003 to August 2017. Zweig Breadth Thrust: about 87 years of breadth history (from 1928 per practitioner sources) [uncertain]
out_of_sample: None found for any TICK rule. CXO: near-term forecasting of market behavior with breadth 'appears futile'; monthly averages somewhat better. Zweig Breadth Thrust: critics report no clear independent out-of-sample validation. Yu, Webb and Lin (2025) tested breadth out of sample per abstract; results not accessible
cost_assumption: None found for any TICK or breadth strategy in the sources reviewed
reported_metrics: No Sharpe, expectancy or win rate reported for TICK rules in the sources. Zweig Breadth Thrust: 10 great, 3 meh and 12 horrible signals (McClellan). CXO: breadth evidence mixed and weak; apparent power depends heavily on 2008-2009. Steenbarger: strong same-day link between advance-decline and price change, but not a tradable forward edge in flat-market days. SentimenTrader: lowering the Zweig threshold to 60 percent deteriorated returns
third_party_replication: None found. TradingView TICK scripts are unverified community work; one author states their TICK strategy is unlikely to be profitable on other tickers or timeframes without re-tuning all parameters
evidence_grade: Pratisyen ozet and community scripts for TICK. Breadth has academic work at abstract level only (Journal of Investing 2025, findings not verified). No hakemli TICK study found
decay_status: Unknown. Ord rule dates from the early 1990s; no post-2010 TICK study found. Market microstructure changed with HFT and ETF flows, which may change TICK behavior [uncertain]
regime_split: Not reported for TICK. CXO: breadth results depend on the 2008-2009 crash. Zweig Breadth Thrust: signals are rare and regime-dependent
data_source_requirement: Real-time NYSE TICK and advance/decline data (NYSE internals). Not in Maven MT5 or Dukascopy [uncertain: not checked on Maven]. Free delayed TICK charts exist on TradingView (TICK.US). Historical intraday TICK requires a paid vendor [uncertain: vendor and price not verified]. Zweig/CXO daily breadth history is available from practitioner sources
min_lot_fit_5k10k: Not computable: no stop rule published. If traded through a US index CFD, the 0.01 lot risk must be computed from the Maven contract specification [uncertain]
fn_rule_fit: Intraday TICK extremes can trigger repeated entries (grid or scalp-like behavior) if not capped; this could conflict with FN tick-scalp and grid restrictions [uncertain]. TICK extremes cluster at the 09:30 open and at 08:30 and 10:00 ET releases, which may fall inside the +-5 minute news window (40 percent rule) [uncertain]. FN rule texts were taken from the task brief and not re-verified
bot_policy_compliance: Automatable only with a live TICK feed (not native to MT5), so an external data connection is needed and must be checked against FN bot policy [uncertain]. No messaging link inherently required
event_overlap: High overlap: TICK extremes concentrate at the 09:30 open, around 08:30 and 10:00 ET macro releases, and in the 15:50 ET closing imbalance window [uncertain: general market knowledge, not from sources]
overlap_with_existing: Conceptual overlap with Sweep (US100 intraday extremes and reversals) is possible; not measured [uncertain]. Donchian XAU: low overlap
rejected_catalog_hit: Not checked against the elenenler catalog. Run `python -m intraday.elenenler --kontrol tick` and `--kontrol breadth` before pre-registration [uncertain]
base_rate_check: No base rate reported. For TICK extremes, the hit rate must be compared with the unconditional up-move probability at the same time of day, which no source provides. Zweig sample of about 25 signals is too small for conditional inference [uncertain]
pitfall_risk: High. (1) Very small sample for breadth thrusts (about 25 signals); (2) parameter sensitivity (threshold 60 vs 61.5 percent changed results; 600 and 1000 TICK levels chosen post hoc); (3) consecutive TICK readings counted as independent observations; (4) no cost model, while open and close TICK extremes carry high spread and slippage; (5) breadth studies dominated by a few crash periods (2008-2009)
priority_score: 1/5. No rigorous evidence for TICK; the signal count is too small for breadth thrusts; the data is not in Maven MT5; revisit only if a historical TICK feed and a pre-registered rule are available
